chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Ralph Burns as Herman's biggest success
summary: Herman calls Ralph Burns his biggest success, with Stan Getz second, and wishes Burns could write new music for the band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And Ralph, of course, he played a dual role for you, mostly both as pianist...
Yeah, and arranger, of course. His arranging ability is beyond anyone's concept, as far as I am concerned. There's no one that ever really touched him.
You want to talk about him at length? It seems that he's a subject that would be --

Well, I think that he's my biggest success. That's The only way I can express it. In other words, of all the people that I've known through my bands, he has gone the farthest and then, too, if I had to put a second one, I'd have to put from the broadness of his approach and his accep-

tance worldwide would be Stan Getz. But I don't think there's a comparison at all, because one man is a completely different kind of person than the other, and I think that -- I feel very strongly that Ralph's music still has not been heard. I would give anything if I were in a position, and he were in a position to spend the time, to write new music for me. Because I think it would probably be the epitome of everything I've done in my whole life, and maybe his, too.
I think we were good for each other.
